title: PGI 208.7401 Definitions
content:
PGI 208.7401 Definitions
L0:As used in this subpart—
L0:“Golden Disk” means a purchased license or entitlement to distribute an unlimited or bulk number of copies of software throughout DoD.
L0:“Software product manager” means the Government official who manages an enterprise software agreement.

title: PGI 208.7403 Acquisition procedures
content:
PGI 208.7403 Acquisition procedures
L2:(1) After requirements are determined, the requiring official must review the information at the ESI website to determine if the required commercial software or related services are available from DoD inventory (e.g., Golden Disks and DoD-wide software maintenance agreements). If the software or services are available, the requiring official must fulfill the requirement from the DoD inventory.
L2:(2) If the required commercial software or related services are not in the DoD inventory, and not on an ESA, the contracting officer or requiring official may fulfill the requirement by other means. Existing ESAs are listed on the ESI website.
L2:(3) If the commercial software or related services are on an ESA, the contracting officer or requiring official must review the terms and conditions and prices in accordance with otherwise applicable source selection requirements.
L2:(4) If an ESA’s terms and conditions and prices represent the best value to the Government, the contracting officer or requiring official must fulfill the requirement for software or services through the ESA.
L2:(5) If existing ESAs do not represent the best value to the Government, the software product manager (SPM) must be given an opportunity to provide the same or a better value to the Government under the ESAs before the contracting officer or requiring official may continue with alternate acquisition methods.
L1:(i) The contracting officer or requiring official must notify the SPM of specific concerns about existing ESA terms and conditions or prices through the ESI webpage.
L3:(ii) The SPM must consider adjusting, within the scope of the ESA, terms and conditions or prices to provide the best value to the customer.
L4:(A) Within 3 working days, the SPM must—
L2:(1) Update the ESA;
L2:(2) Provide an estimated date by which the update will be accomplished; or
L2:(3) Inform the contracting officer or requiring official that no change will be made to the ESA.
L4:(B) If the SPM informs the contracting officer or requiring official that no change will be made to the ESA terms and conditions or prices, the contracting officer or requiring official may fulfill the requirement by other means.
L4:(C) If the SPM does not respond within 3 working days or does not plan to adjust the ESA within 90 days, the contracting officer or requiring official may fulfill the requirement by other means.
L3:(iii) A management official designated by the department or agency may waive the requirement to obtain commercial software or related services through an ESA after the steps in paragraphs (5)(i) and (5)(ii)(A) of this section are complete. The rationale for use of an alternate source must be included in the waiver request and must be provided to the SPM.

title: PGI 270.104 Procedures
content:
PGI 270.104 Procedures
L1:(a) Contracting officers may submit applications for participation in the pilot program to OUSD(A&S), Defense Pricing, Contracting, and Acquisition Policy (DPCAP) (Contract Policy) (DPCAP/CP) via email at osd.pentagon.ousd-a-s.mbx.dpc-cp@mail.mil. The application must include the following:
L2:(1) The cognizant contracting activity, including the department or agency, command, awarding contract office, and program office.
L2:(2) A copy of the predecessor contract and modifications, except funding and administrative modifications, and indicate if such contract was awarded pursuant to DFARS 270.1.
L2:(3) A description of the proposed follow-on requirement, including the product or service, quantity, and period of performance.
L2:(4) The anticipated contract value.
L2:(5) A copy of any waiver(s) issued.
L1:(b) DPCAP/CP will respond to the contracting officer within 30 days of receipt of the application.
L1:(c) Contracting officers must not issue a solicitation prior to receipt of DPCAP/CP approval of participation in this pilot program.
L1:(d) Not later than 60 days after the end of the period of performance of the contract, the contracting activity must submit to DPCAP/CP via email to osd.pentagon.ousd-a-s.mbx.dpc-cp@mail.mil—
L2:(1) The contractor’s response submitted to the contracting officer pursuant to the clause at DFARS 252.270-7002, Pilot Program to Incentivize Contracting with Employee-Owned Businesses; and
L2:(2) Information from the contracting officer as follows:
L3:(i) Summary of contractor performance on the predecessor contract.
L3:(ii) Summary of contractor performance on the follow-on contract.
L3:(iii) Identification and discussion of any benefits or disadvantages the contracting activity, department, or agency experienced using the pilot program.
L3:(iv) Any best practices the department or agency implemented as a result of the pilot program.
L3:(v) Any other information the department or agency would like to share regarding its experience utilizing the pilot program.
